title: Coupe parcel shelf removal and installation
introduction:
The coupe’s parcel shelf comes out after the surrounding trim has been released. I treat this as a trim jigsaw: finding each hidden attachment beats arm-wrestling the plastic. The route runs through the loadspace side panels, then the D-pillar panels, and finally the shelf.

The supporting instructions below explain the weatherstrip, scuff-plate and rear-seat access needed along the way. Use the illustrations to locate the clips, separate tether attachment and shelf retainers. This procedure applies to the coupe with a rear seat fitted; it does not cover a rear-seat-delete configuration.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service around the vehicle. Otherwise, it could start remotely at any time and cause personal injury or death. With the car parked and the parking brake applied, move both front seats fully forward for rear-cushion access before beginning trim removal. Then switch the ignition OFF and remove the vehicle key to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use the required protection can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Illustration applicability
items.detail: The supporting loadspace-trim procedure shows LHD; RHD is similar. It shows the RH side; the LH side is similar. Complete the required trim removal on both sides.

items.name: Rear-seat cushion referral
items.detail: Use [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168) (501-10B Rear Seats, Removal and Installation) for the cushion-removal prerequisite. Its supplied release method is explained with the loadspace-panel step below.

items.name: Protect the cushion locking tabs
items.detail: Press the seat-cushion locking tabs inward to release them from the floor before lifting the cushion. Lifting without pressing the tabs inward can damage them.

items.name: Seat-belt routing
items.detail: During reassembly of the loadspace trim and rear-seat cushion, make sure the safety-belt webbing is not twisted and all belts and buckles remain accessible to the occupants.

edits.text: Remove the loadspace trim panels on both sides. Refer to: [Loadspace Trim Panel - Coupe](#/document/G1692601) (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: These panels are the first layer in the access sequence. On each side, position the door weatherstrip aside, then release the clips and remove the scuff plate trim panel; its illustration shows upward release. Next, remove the rear-seat cushion: with both front seats already fully forward from preparation, press inward on the locking tabs at the front of the rear cushion to release it from the floor, then lift, release and remove the cushion. Pressing the tabs first prevents tab damage. Release the rear-backrest latch and lower the backrest. Finally, position the safety-belt guide aside, release the loadspace-panel clips and remove the panel. Work along the loadspace panel’s top edge, its rear vertical edge beside the lowered backrest, and its forward lower foot beside the sill to release the attachments. Pull the freed panel inward away from the body, keeping the belt webbing clear. The front seats are moved for access, not removed.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustration shows the RH side; the LH side is similar.
edits.why: Use the pictured attachment arrangement to guide the corresponding work on the opposite side.

edits.text: On both sides, release the D-pillar trim-panel clips, disconnect the tether clip, then remove the panel.
edits.why: The inset shows the retaining clips and the separate tether attachment. I check that tether before treating the panel as free—it can still be on its leash after the other clips release.

edits.text: Remove the pin-type retainers at the ends of the parcel shelf, then remove the shelf in the direction shown.
edits.why: The magenta highlights locate the retainers, while the arrows across the blue shelf indicate its removal movement. Removing the retainers frees the shelf for that movement.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order. Refit the parcel shelf and pin-type retainers, reconnect the D-pillar tether clips and retaining clips, then reinstall the loadspace panels and their access parts. During reassembly, keep the safety-belt webbing untwisted and the belts and buckles accessible to the occupants.
edits.why: Reversing the sequence restores the trim layers and their attachments. The loadspace-panel and rear-cushion instructions both call out belt routing: a tidy-looking cabin is only finished when the occupants can reach and use the belts. Refit the loadspace trim and restore its safety-belt guides, raise and latch the rear backrest, and refit the cushion with its front locking tabs engaged in the floor. Refit the scuff plates and restore the displaced door weatherstrips, then return the front seats to their desired positions. Confirm the webbing stays untwisted and every belt and buckle remains accessible.
